The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident that occurred on 22-09-2023.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 22-09-2023 at about 12.30 p.m. the petitioner was boarding the stopped BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 at Jai Bharath Nagara Bus Stop, Jai Bharath nagara,

Bangalore, at that time the driver of the said bus without closing the front door, nor watching the side mirror and whether the passengers boarded inside the bus,
suddenly moved the bus ahead in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the left side stopped another BMTC bus and caused the accident.

Due to the impact,
the petitioner stricken in between both BMTC buses and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Sundar hospital,
Lingarajapuram, Bangalore, after first aid treatment injured was shifted to Baptist hospital, wherein the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and discharged with an advice of regular followup treatment and bed rest.
Petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 55 years and was doing flower vending work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue with her work and lost her income.
The respondent is the owner and internal insurer of the bus and is liable to pay compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.

3. After service of notice respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by contending that, on 22-09-2023 the BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 was on its schedule trip from K R Puram to reach K R Market bus station, Route No.3040/1, when the said bus was stopped at Jaibharathnagar bus stop, the petitioner tried to open the middle door of the said bus and attempted to board the bus, but the door was half opened and due to which the petitioner stuck in the middle of the door and caused the accident.
Hence the petitioner herself contributed towards the cause of accident.
Further it has denied the contention of the petitioner that, the driver of the said BMTC bus dashed on the left side portion of the stopped another BMTC bus.
Further it has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also the injuries sustained by her due to the accident, treatment taken and amount spent towards medical expenses.
Hence, the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court at the time of pronouncement of judgment :
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she has sustained griev- ous injuries due to the actionable neg- ligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 by its driver, in RTA took place on 22-09-2023 at about 12.30 p.m. at Jai Bharath Nagara bus stop, Jai Bharath Nagar, Bengaluru?
2.
Whether the petitioner is enti- tled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 10, 13 & 14.
Further the Dr. R Kantharaju, Orthopedic surgeon is examined as PW.2 and through him Ex.P11 & 12 were got marked.

On the other hand the driver of the bus is examined as RW.1 and Ex.R1 is got marked.
6.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-

 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed her affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of her case, she has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, spot mahazar along with sketch which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 5 & 10.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1, FIR which is registered on the basis of the first information given by the petitioner herself by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.
KA.57.F.2308.

The contents of Ex.P2 complaint and Ex.P1 FIR supports the contention of the petitioner about the rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 which is owned and insured by the respondent.
In continuation of Ex.P1 & 2, the police drawn spot mahazar and rough sketch which are marked as Ex.P10.

On perusal of Ex.P10 the accident spot is in the BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 was shown to be stopped in the right side portion of the road and not on the extreme left side which is near to the bus stop.

As per the Ex.P10 spot mahazar and rough sketch the BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.3265 has stopped exactly near to the BMTC Bus Stop in the left side edge of the road but whereas the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.
KA.57.F.2308 stopped his bus not in the left side edge but in the right side portion of the road behind BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.3265.

If the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 stopped his bus near to the BMTC bus stop in the left side edge of the road and thereafter opened the door of his bus the said accident is not going to be caused.

The major negligence of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 was he stopped his bus behind the another bus in the right side portion of the road wherein enough space was available to stop his bus in the left side edge of the road.

Thereby the rough sketch establishes that the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.
KA.57.F.2308 stopped his bus in right side portion of the road which resulted in the said accident.

The contents of Ex.P10 helped the petitioner to prove the negligence of the BMTC Bus bearing No.

10.

sentences.text: It is very important to note that the respondent in its written statement admitted the accident but contended that, while the bus was moving the petitioner tried to open the middle door of the bus and attempted to get in to the moving bus from middle automatic door in due course lost the control and stuck in between the doors and sustained grievous injuries.
Thereby it is admitted before this tribunal that the petitioner has got injuries in the RTA dated 22-09-2023 which involves the BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308.
But the rough sketch establishes the negligence of driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 who stopped his bus in the right side portion and not in left side edge of the road.

11. The charge sheet as per Ex.P5 is filed against the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing No.
KA.57.F.2308 wherein the IO opined that rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 was the sole reason for the accident.
No grounds are made out to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
"12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants''.

Hence, by relying on the said precedent and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 5 & 10, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308.
12.
Admittedly, the petitioner got injuries while she was boarding to bus.
If the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 closed the middle automatic door before moving the bus the petitioner was not going to fell down and got injuries in the accident.
The middle automatic door was not closed and itself is the major negligence of the bus driver.

Further no other eye witnesses are examined by the respondent to show that the driver of the bus closed the door and moved the bus after the due instructions from the conductor or by observing in the mirror.
It is the duty of the driver and conductor to close the door and thereafter shall move the bus.

But in this case, it shows that the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 tried to move the bus while the petitioner Rathnamma vs B.M.T.C on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58920723/
4 was boarding the bus.

This shows that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 and no grounds are made out by the respondent to show the contributory negligence of the petitioner.
13.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
15. As per well settled principle of law the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence there are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner.

All the materials available on record leading to show that,
petitioner sustained injuries in the accident took place on 22-09-2023 which is caused by the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 which belongs to the respondent.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
16.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that she has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.57.F.2308 belongs to respondent.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
(A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.4 - wound certificate, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained severe injuries which are grievous in nature.
Petitioner has also produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P6.

On perusal of the same it reveals that the petitioner has taken treatment at Bangalore Baptist hospital from 23-09-2023 to 04-10-2023 and has sustained Bilateral pneumothorax, bilateral lung contusion, bilateral multiple rib fractures, bilateral pubic rami fracture, grade 2 liver laceration and L1-L5 transverse process fracture.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in wound certificate and discharge summary, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.80,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:

5

sentences.text: The petitioner has contended that she has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- for her treatment and has produced medical bills which are marked at Ex.P7 & 13.
These bills are not disputed by the respondent and no grounds are made out to disbelieving this bill.

But in the Sl. No.35 bill of Ex.P7 the total amount of the inpatient bill was Rs.1,40,577/- out of which Rs.27,985/- was shown as discount and only Rs.1,12,590/-
(Rs.80,000/- + 32,950/-) was paid by the petitioner.
For the Sl No.35 bill only Rs.1,12,590/- shall be reimbursed along with other medical bills.
The Sl.37 & 38 of Ex.P7 cannot be reimbursed as these bills are in the name of one Nagaraj.

The total amount of the other medical bills produced at Ex.P7 & 13 is Rs.1,87,285/- Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.1,87,300/- under this head.

C)
Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that she was doing flower vending work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any documents.
In the absence of evidence the notional income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.16,000/- as the accident is of the year 2023.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P6 the petitioner was admitted to Bangalore Baptist hospital from 23-09-2023 to 04-10-2023 for a period of 11 days.
Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered.
Hence, the 4 months of period is considered as healing period including 11 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months = Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.
d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by her the petitioner examined Dr. R Kantharaju as PW.2, through him clinical notes and X- ray are marked at Ex.P.11 & 12.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner has sustained Bilateral pneumothorax, bilateral lung contusion, bilateral multiple rib fractures, bilateral pubic rami fracture, grade 2 liver laceration and L1-L5 transverse process fracture.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered total disability of 24.99% to the whole body.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
No other expert evidence are adduced by the respondent to disprove the alleged disability stated by PW.2 doctor.
According to the petitioner she was doing flower vending work and sustained grievous injuries.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on her occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 19% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P14.
As per the Ex.P14 the year of birth of the petitioner is 1968.
The accident was occurred in the year 2023.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 55 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '11'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 11 X 19% =Rs. 4,01,280/- which is the total loss of future income.

6 e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;

entities.text: Rathnamma vs B.M.T.C on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Ex.P6 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 11 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period she spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained she is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 11 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.11,000/- in total.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by her, which might certainly have deprived her of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 80,000/- b.

Towards medical expenses Rs. 1,87,300/-
c.

Towards loss of income during Rs. 64,000/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 4,01,280/- e.

Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 50,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 11,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 60,000/-
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent is the owner and there is a internal insurance to the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
18.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner, 50% shall be released to petitioner on proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
